defects.description: Found while building MCE-07: the mapping-driven adapter lets the provider write the status_normalization table, which is right for a vendor's private vocabulary (AUD-F70 protects the unmapped case). XCCDF's result vocabulary is not a vendor's: the standard defines notchecked as not evaluated, error as a tool failure, fixed as 'had failed, but was then fixed' with no re-check implied, and notapplicable as not applying. Through the generic path a provider table could relabel any of them PASS, or omit `fail` so that failures fell to the unmapped rule and read as UNKNOWN, and the adapter would have accepted it. A benchmark scan also reports every rule in the benchmark, so the MCE-02 rule that an undeclared check refuses the whole batch would have forced a provider to declare every rule to KSIs, draining the declaration of meaning, or to pre-filter the scanner output by hand.
defects.root_cause: MCE-02 was designed for exports whose vocabulary and record set the provider controls; a standardized results format controls both.

The maintainer's real practice was read from the tags: v1.5.0 and v1.6.0 are SSH-signed (SSHSIG v1, namespace git, sha512) by one ed25519 key, fingerprint SHA256:95T8oBQ46qClD/NUDTlUsP6hxVKCLDsfjMJtsZY5wAY, extracted from the signature blobs and matched to the maintainer's configured public signing key; v1.4.0 and earlier carry no signature, as the workflow header already records.

defects.requirement: The release gate must establish not only WHO signed the tag (AUD-F88) but WHY that signer is trusted. A trust anchor read from the artifact under judgement is not an anchor: the allowed-signers file must be one that reached the protected branch through its required status check, and the gate must prove that before consulting it.

defects.description: Found by an external re-audit of main ffb3b55 (2026-10-19) and confirmed verbatim: the verify-tag job read SIGNERS=.github/release-allowed-signers from its own checkout of the tagged commit and bound the tag only to GITHUB_SHA (event-to-tag consistency), never to protected main. With no tag ruleset (the rulesets API returns an empty set) any identity able to push a commit and a v* tag could place its own public key in that commit's signers file, sign the tag with the matching private key, and pass `git verify-tag`; a passing run then reaches the publish job, which holds contents: write and creates the GitHub Release. The repository's only collaborator today is the owner, so the exposure is a single compromised credential rather than an insider, but the gate claimed a property it did not hold. Reproduced in a throwaway clone under bash with the step's shell extracted verbatim: an attacker branch carrying its own signer list, tagged and signed by the attacker key, passed every check up to the manifest binding on the pre-fix shell.
defects.root_cause: AUD-F88 fixed the cryptographic operation but left the trust anchor inside the tagged commit's tree, with nothing relating that commit to the protected branch whose review process is what makes the signers file trustworthy.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- the verify-tag step fetches main by its own ref (`git fetch --no-tags origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, so the comparison target comes from the server's branch protection and never from the tag), requires `git merge-base --is-ancestor $tag_commit refs/remotes/origin/main` and fails closed naming the commit otherwise, and does so BEFORE the signers file is read or gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile is set; the branch name is one env value (PROTECTED_BRANCH). Every F88 check follows unchanged. The workflow header records the reasoning and docs/versioning.md names main's branch protection as part of the release trust chain. The tag ruleset (restrict v* creation/update/deletion) is a repository setting the owner applies; it is recommended beside this fix, not a substitute for it
